name: Lithium
role: Mobile cation (Li+) — the working ion in Li6PS5Cl argyrodite; also the Li-metal anode. Occupies partially-filled 48h/24g cage sites; hops through the PS4/halide framework. Ionic, closed-shell (2s0 as Li+).

ionic_radius_A._note: Shannon 1976 effective ionic radii; VI (octahedral) 0.76 A, IV (tetrahedral) 0.59 A. Argyrodite Li sits in distorted tetrahedral/triangular cage sites.

representative_compounds.battery_role: Li-metal negative electrode; plating/stripping substrate for SEI
representative_compounds.note: Li0; argyrodite is thermodynamically reduced against Li metal (reduction onset ~1.7 V vs Li/Li+, Bai 2020 review) -> forms Li2S + Li3P + LiCl interphase

representative_compounds.battery_role: reduction product of the S sublattice; also conversion-cathode active material and Li reservoir
representative_compounds.note: Electronically insulating but a soft, Li+-conductive SEI phase; forms with LiCl+Li3P on argyrodite reduction

representative_compounds.battery_role: terminal reduction product of PS4 3- against Li metal (P in -3 state)
representative_compounds.note: Diagnostic: drives P 2p3/2 down to ~125.4 eV (see P.json). Mixed Li3P-Li2S solid solutions proposed as fully-reduced SE for Li anodes (PMC9479069)

representative_compounds.battery_role: wide-gap insulating passivator from Cl sublattice reduction; blocks electron transfer while passing Li+
representative_compounds.note: Cl-rich argyrodite gives LiCl-rich SEI (Liu 2022); wide gap ~6-6.6 eV -> self-limiting passivation logic
Reference intercalation host; contrasts with plating on bare Li metal

representative_compounds.battery_role: very low Li+ migration barrier; anode interlayer candidate
representative_compounds.note: CAMPAIGN RULE: UMA MLIP is FORBIDDEN for Li3N (2026-06 deterministic-bias ruling) — use DFT/AIMD, not UMA, for any Li3N energetics

sei_relevance: Li metal anode is the SEI-forming electrode. Argyrodite is not stable vs Li: reduced (~1.7 V vs Li/Li+) to a Li2S + Li3P + LiCl interphase. Because these are wide-gap insulators (LiCl ~6-6.6, Li2O ~5.2, Li2S), the SEI is electronically blocking but Li+-conductive -> a self-limiting/passivating layer that widens the effective electrochemical window beyond the thermodynamic prediction. Li 1s XPS is a weak chemical-state probe (see xps); SEI phase ID relies on the anion core levels (S 2p, Cl 2p, P 2p).

xps.ref: Wood & Teeter, ACS Appl. Energy Mater. 2018

xps.assignment: LiF / Li2CO3 / LixPOyFz region (~55-60 eV); Li2S also ~55
xps.ref: ACS Energy Lett. 2022 SEI XPS primer

xps.assignment: NOTE: total Li 1s chemical shift across SEI phases is only ~3-5 eV and peaks overlap -> Li 1s alone poorly discriminates SEI; use O 1s/S 2p/Cl 2p/P 2p and BE separations

raman.assignment: Li2S (SEI reduction-product marker; appears when PS4 framework is damaged vs Li)
raman.ref: Ke et al., Energy Storage Mater. 2025

raman.assignment: NOTE: metallic Li and ionic Li+ are not Raman-diagnostic; Li environments are tracked indirectly via framework (PS4) and SEI (Li2S) modes

dos_character: Li is essentially ionic (Li+): it donates its 2s electron to the framework and contributes little density of states at the band edges. In Li6PS5Cl the VBM is S 3p (non-bonding S lone pairs) and the CBM is PS4 antibonding + a minor Li 2s/2p admixture; Li 1s is a deep, inert core level. Consequently Li acts as a rigid-band electron donor / carrier, not a redox center.
